messages:
devon: quick brain dump — i'm drafting an RFC to converge hosted/dedicated/private runtime APIs into a single 'runtime contract'. want to nail the minimal required surface and explicit extension points. do we try to standardize health/metrics/telemetry too? thoughts?

alice: +1 on a single contract for inference requests. but we should separate control-plane lifecycle APIs from the inference path. mixing them adds blast radius for private.

ben: agreed. inference request should be tiny: model, input, flags, routing hints. lifecycle (provision, scale, register) can be separate with stricter auth.

carolina: we also need a capability discovery endpoint so clients can query features per deployment (quantization, max_seq, kv_cache_support). that avoids brittle feature-detection.

devon: capability discovery sounds good. propose /capabilities and a short JSON fingerprint that includes supported ops + limits.

alice: example for /capabilities:
```json
{
  "runtime_version": "1.2",
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "supports_streaming": true,
  "quant_profiles": ["int8", "gptq"],
  "kv_cache": true
}
```

ben: for auth: hosted uses our bearer tokens; dedicated/private need tokens issued by customer SSO or delegated creds. contract should allow multiple auth schemes but require presence of an 'auth_type' header.

carolina: +1. also add KMS hint metadata (e.g., kms_key_id) for private. but make it optional for hosted.

devon: okay — minimal inference request body (proposal):
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-xl-1",
  "input": "...",
  "runtime_version": "v1",
  "routing_hint": "region:us-east-1;prefer:hosted",
  "metadata": {"kms_key_id": "optional"}
}
```

alice: keep metadata freeform but recommend standard keys in the spec. avoid deep nesting to keep proxies/lightweight gateways happy.

ben: on metrics/telemetry: include a required set of tags on every request response for internal metrics: deployment_type, region, model, runtime_version. everything else optional. this lets Console aggregate across modes.

carolina: should those be headers or in-body? headers are easier for edge proxies, but body keeps things explicit and signed. leaning headers: X-RW-Deployment-Type, X-RW-Region, X-RW-Model.

devon: headers it is. we'll require canonical header names and document them. also add a signed body header for private when customer requires attestation.

ben: fallback policies: we need a compact policy format clients can pass or servers can suggest. example: `prefer:[hosted,dedicated], fallback_to_private:false, on_failure:503`

carolina: warn: we must avoid cross-tenant side-effects. private deployments cannot allow hosted to pull model weights or cache them unless customer explicitly permits. include explicit capability bit `allow_remote_caching`.

alice: agreed. policy surface should be orthogonal to data residency. separate flags for caching, telemetry_sharing, and model_sync.

devon: thoughts on health checks and readiness? keep a common path `/healthz` with structured status: {ok:true, uptime_s, active_sessions}, plus a `detail_url` for private where we can surface local reasons.

ben: yes — but healthz must not leak internal topology. for private, `detail_url` should be behind customer auth. return generic status to public clients.

carolina: versioning: require `X-RW-Runtime-Version` header. SDKs must tolerate unknown future fields. we should also publish a capability-compatibility matrix.

devon: rollout plan question — do we gate the unified contract behind a feature flag for dedicated/customers? we can't force private infra to upgrade instantly.

alice: support discovery of the highest common denominator. SDK attempts to talk v1; if server replies with unsupported_capability, SDK fallbacks to legacy path. no hard break.

ben: and we should add a lightweight manifest for private deployments that gets uploaded to control plane during onboarding: `deployment_manifest.json` (contains capabilities, region, public_endpoints, allowed_kms_patterns).

carolina: logging/PII: require guidance that hosted strips customer PII by default unless opt-in, and private keeps logs locally. contract should include a `pii_policy` enum: [strip, redact, keep] that deployments advertise in /capabilities.

devon: excellent. last bit: SDK ergonomics — keep single client surface but allow `client.overrideDeployment({type:\"private\", endpoint:\"...\"})` so apps can switch targets without code change.

alice: small security note: TLS + mTLS for private control-plane. require explicit client cert header if mTLS used. document fallback to token-based only if configured.

infra-bot: deploy-job #4242: started rollout of runtime-contract v0.9 to staging (eng-rt). :rocket:

devon: thanks infra-bot. next steps: i'll draft RFC with these concrete bullets: minimal inference body, capability endpoint, header conventions, minimal metrics tags, control-plane vs data-plane separation, opt-in caching bits, privacy flags, and graceful SDK downgrade. will ping here when draft ready.

oncall-bot: Reminder: arch sync Friday 10:00 — put RFC on agenda.

carolina: looks good. i'll add a short diagram of control vs data plane in the RFC. would be helpful to show where policies live.

ben: can we include a short compatibility table for legacy hosted endpoints? i can sketch it.

alice: +1. also include a tiny example of a canary rollout: bind hosted -> dedicated for 10% traffic, automatic fallback.

devon: cool — thanks all. I'll post draft by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
